rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excerpt preserves an unidentified battle poem describing a praised warrior as armor-filling when called to combat and pressed by fear; its preceding lexical context is not included.
rows.anchor: ولنعم حشو الدرع أنت إذا ... دعيت نزال ولج في الذعر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He glosses the condemned support as the people’s aid: the worldly curse sustains their punishment, and an afterlife curse adds to it.
rows.anchor: بئس الرفد المرفود رفدهم، أي: بئس العون المعان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He also offers “a bad gift given” as a possible gloss of the condemned support.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بئس العطاء المعطى انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes al-Zamakhshari’s syntax to make «المرفود» an adjective of «الرفد», with the condemned item omitted and understood as their aid.
rows.anchor: المرفود صفة للرفد، وأن المخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره: رفدهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: The interpretation “bad aid that is aided” is Abu ʿUbayda’s gloss; punishment is called support metaphorically, as in calling a painful blow a greeting.
rows.anchor: هو قول أبي عبيدة، وسمي العذاب رفدا على نحو قولهم تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes «الرفد» as hospitality or provision: after drowning, the Fire is the wretched thing they are given.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الرفد الرفادة أي بئس ما يرفدون به بعد الغرق النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points back to the prophets, their peoples, and the punishments just recounted: this is some of the history of the towns.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بذلك إلى ما تقدم من ذكر الأنبياء وقومهم، وما حل بهم من العقوبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns may be the particular communities already destroyed, or towns generally: their story is the recurring pattern when cities disbelieve, including contemporary cities.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يعنى بالقرى قرى أولئك المهلكين المتقدم ذكرهم، وأن يعني القرى عموما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in «منها» refers to the towns.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منها عائد على القرى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On the general reading of “towns,” he glosses «قائم وحصيد» as inhabited and vanished, exemplified by Zughar and Dathir.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قائم وحصيد عامر كزغر وداثر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: With Ibn Jurayj, he reads the specific destroyed towns as having standing walls or being collapsed.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وابن جريج: قائم الجدران ومنهدم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He describes some towns as remaining and others as erased in trace, like standing grain and harvested grain; Abu Hayyan identifies this with Qatada’s interpretation.
rows.anchor: بعضها باق وبعضها عافي الأثر كالزرع القائم على ساقه، والذي حصد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He also glosses the pair as a trace still standing versus one erased, using harvest as a metaphor for extinction.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: قائم الأثر ودارسه، جعل حصد الزرع كناية عن الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited, unidentified poem compares people divided by death to standing and harvested crops, evidencing the crop metaphor.
rows.anchor: والناس في قسم المنية بينهم ... كالزرع منه قائم وحصيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says «قائم» is not swallowed by the earth, while «حصيد» has been swallowed.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: قائم لم يخسف، وحصيد قد خسف

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets «قائم» as not yet destroyed and «حصيد» as already destroyed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: قائم لم يهلك بعد، وحصيد قد أهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes «قائم» and «حصيد» of surviving versus cut-off descendants; it suits an implied “people of the towns,” whose omission is supported by the following pronoun “them.”
rows.anchor: قائم أي باق نسله، وحصيد أي منقطع نسله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses «حصيد» as passive «محصود» and gives its plural forms as «حصدى» and «حصاد».
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: حصيد أي محصود، وجمعه حصدى وحصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pattern «فعلى» can pluralize an active participle in passive sense only for rational beings, as in «قتيل» and «قتلى».
rows.anchor: وباب فعلى جمعا لفعيل بمعنى مفعول، أن يكون فيمن يعقل نحو: قتيل وقتلى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He treats «ذلك من أنباء القرى نقصه عليك» as a resumptive sentence with no syntactic position.
rows.anchor: قلت: هي مستأنفة لا محل لها انتهى

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ makes «منها قائم» an initial nominal clause serving circumstantially for the pronoun in «نقصه», and supplies «ومنها حصيد» with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: منها قائم ابتداء، وخبر في موضع الحال من الهاء في نقصه، وحصيد مبتدأ خبره محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls that parse loose; the sense is that the towns are in this condition as God recounts them, a circumstantial construction that more forcefully warns and exemplifies for contemporaries who can see God’s acts.
rows.anchor: والحال أبلغ في التخويف وضرب المثل للحاضرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not wrong the towns by destroying them; He imposed only the punishment they deserved, while they wronged themselves by choosing disbelief over faith and committing what led to ruin.
rows.anchor: وما ظلمناهم أي: بإهلاكنا إياهم، بل وضعنا عليهم من العذاب ما يستحقونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is a denial that the idols averted any of God’s might or benefited their worshippers.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: فما أغنت، نفي أي، لم ترد عنهم من بأس الله شيئا ولا أجدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «يدعون» narrates their former practice, meaning that they used to worship or invoke the idols such as al-Lat, al-ʿUzza, and Hubal.
rows.anchor: يدعون حكاية حال أي: التي كانوا يدعون، أي يعبدون، أو يدعونها اللات والعزى وهبل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses «لما» as an adverb governed by «أغنت»; Abu Hayyan says this conflicts with Sibawayh, who treats it as a particle expressing one event’s obligation after another.
rows.anchor: ولما منصوب بما أغنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «أمر ربك» means God’s punishment and vengeance.
rows.anchor: وأمر ربك هو عذابه ونقمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols receive a rational plural pronoun because their worshippers treated them as rational beings, believing them beneficial and worshipping them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم نزلوهم منزلة العقلاء في اعتقادهم أنها تنفع، وعبادتهم إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «التتبيب» means causing loss; the reported glosses of evil, ruin, and destruction are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: والتتبيب التخسير

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses «التتبيب» as evil.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: الشر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses «التتبيب» as loss and destruction.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الخسران والهلاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses «التتبيب» as causing loss.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: التخسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further gloss takes «التتبيب» as destruction; Abu Hayyan says all these interpretations are close.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التدمير. وهذه كلها أقوال متقاربة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says idols increase their followers’ loss by occupying them with hope, trust, and worship instead of reflection on revelation and its outcome; alternatively, punishment for disbelief is increased by the added offense of idolatry.
rows.anchor: وصورة زيادة الأصنام التتبيب، إنما هو يتصور بأن تأميلها والثقة بها والتعب في عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning applies generally to unjust towns; wrongdoing includes disbelief and other injustices. God may delay some disbelievers, while wrongdoers are usually punished promptly.
rows.anchor: والقرى عام في القرى الظالمة، والظلم يشمل ظلم الكفر وغيره

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء
rows.claim: Abu Rajaʾ and al-Jahdari read «إذ أخذ» with the first verb perfect and «إذ» as a past-time adverb, reporting God’s established practice of destroying earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء والجحدري: وكذلك أخذ ربك، إذ أخذ

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads «أحذ» in «وكذلك ... ربك»; Abu Hayyan reports the variant without supplying further analysis here.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف: وكذلك أحذ ربك إذا أخذ

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says Talha’s reading is semantically apt, while the canonical reading sustains the warning through time by using a future form for a past event, the usual construction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهي قراءة متمكنة المعنى، ولكن قراءة الجماعة تعطي الوعيد واستمراره في الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object «القرى» is governed by the second of the competing verbs «أخذ ربك» and «أخذ»; «وهي ظالمة» is a circumstantial clause, and «إن أخذه أليم» means the destructive seizure is painful and hard on its victims.
rows.anchor: والقرى مفعول بأخذ على الإعمال إذ تنازعه المصدر وهو: أخذ ربك، وأخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of earlier peoples’ destruction is a sign for those fearing the afterlife: worldly punishment for rejecting messengers and associating partners makes afterlife punishment in the realm of recompense all the more fitting.
rows.anchor: إنهم إذا عذبوا في الدنيا لأجل تكذيبهم الأنبياء وإشراكهم بالله، وهي دار العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets foretold the eradication of those who rejected them, and its fulfillment verifies their reports of resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: ووقع ما أخبروا به وفق إخبارهم، فدل على أن ما أخبروا به من البعث والجزاء صدق لا شك فيه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the account a lesson: worldly punishments are a sample of the afterlife punishment, prompting reflection, greater piety, and fear of God.
rows.anchor: لآية لمن خاف لعبرة له، لأنه ينظر إلى ما أحل الله بالمجرمين في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In «إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى», «ذلك» points to the Day of Resurrection indicated by «عذاب الآخرة».
rows.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى يوم القيامة الدال عليه قوله: عذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In «يوم مجموع له الناس», «الناس» is the passive subject raised by «مجموع».
rows.anchor: والناس مفعول لم يسم فاعله رافعه مجموع

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows «الناس» as the subject and «مجموع» as a fronted predicate, but Abu Hayyan considers the parse remote and notes it would call for plural «مجموعون».
rows.anchor: وأجاز ابن عطية أن يكون الناس مبتدأ، ومجموع خبر مقدم، وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «مجموع له الناس» denotes the gathering for Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ومجموع له الناس عبارة عن الحشر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say the witnessed Day is attended by all earlier and later humans, jinn, angels, and animals.
rows.anchor: ومشهود عام يشهده الأولون والآخرون من الإنس والجن والملائكة والحيوان في قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God gives a wrongdoer respite, but when He seizes him He does not let him escape; the Prophet then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «إن الله يملي للظالم حتى إذا أخذه لم يفلته»

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the passive participle «مجموع» conveys a fixed, appointed gathering and a lasting quality for the Day and its people more strongly than a finite verb.
rows.anchor: لما في اسم المفعول من دلالته على ثبات معنى الجمع لليوم، وأنه لا بد أن يكون ميعادا مضروبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «مشهود» means witnessed on that Day; the preposition is expanded and the verb reaches its pronoun as though it were a direct object.
rows.anchor: ومعنى مشهود، مشهود فيه، فاتسع في الجار والمجرور ووصل الفعل إلى الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem cited as grammatical evidence says “a day we witnessed,” illustrating the expanded construction; its poet is not identified in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: ويوما شهدناه سليما وعامرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is that creatures witness the gathering place and no one is absent; common phrases likewise describe a gathering as witnessed or a meal as attended.
rows.anchor: يشهد فيه الخلائق الموقف لا يغيب عنه أحد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Day is not called witnessed in itself as in the verse about witnessing the month, because that would not distinguish it from other witnessed days; the intended distinction is its terror and grandeur.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يجعل اليوم مشهودا في نفسه كما قال: فمن شهد منكم الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «نؤخره» refers to that Day; al-Hufi instead says it refers to recompense.
rows.anchor: وما نؤخره أي: ذلك اليوم. وقيل: يعود على الجزاء قاله الحوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fixed term is a prior decree with a set limit that can neither be advanced nor delayed.
rows.anchor: إلا لأجل معدود أي لقضاء سابق قد نفذ فيه بأجل محدود لا يتقدم عليه ولا يتأخر عنه

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads «يؤخره» with a yāʾ instead of «نؤخره».
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: وما يؤخره بالياء

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: The two grammarians and Nafiʿ retain the yāʾ of «يأتي» in connected recitation and drop it at pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النحويان ونافع: يأتي بإثبات الياء وصلا، وحذفها وقفا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir retains the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation; it is also present in Ubayy’s codex.
rows.anchor: وابن كثير بإثباتها وصلا ووقفا، وهي ثابتة في مصحف أبي

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The other canonical readers omit the yāʾ in both connection and pause; it is absent from the Uthmanic codex.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة بحذفها وصلا ووقفا، وسقطت في مصحف الإمام عثمان

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads «يأتون»; the same form appears in ʿAbd Allah’s codex.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش يأتون، وكذا في مصحف عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan regards retaining the yāʾ in connection and pause as preferable; deletion only at pause follows verse endings, while deletion in both positions eases pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وإثباتها وصلا ووقفا هو الوجه، ووجه حذفها في الوقف التشبيه بالفواصل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says using the kasra instead of a yāʾ is common in Hudhayl, and cites a line as evidence.
rows.anchor: الاجتزاء بالكسرة عن الياء كثير في لغة هذيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari’s cited poem illustrates the Hudhayli substitution by ending «درهما» with a kasra in place of the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: كفاك كف ما يليق درهما ... جودا وأخرى تعط بالسيف الدما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent subject of «يأتي» is the Day referred to by «نؤخره» and «ذلك يوم»; «لا تكلم» governs it, meaning no soul speaks that day except by God’s permission, as in another Qurʾanic passage.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الفاعل بيأتي ضمير يعود على ما عاد عليه الضمير في نؤخره

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the subject of «يأتي» to be God, citing passages about God’s coming and the coming of His command; the yāʾ reading «يؤخره» supports this parse.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون فاعل يأتي ضميرا عائدا على الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He also allows «يوم يأتي» to be governed by an implied “remember,” or by the omitted ending of the fixed term: the term ends when that Day arrives.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أيضا أن ينتصب يوم يأتي باذكر أو بالانتهاء المحذوف

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hufi parses «لا تكلم نفس» as a circumstantial clause referring to the Day in «مشهود» or as an adjective of the indefinite «يوم», with «فيه» understood.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الحوفي أن يكون لا تكلم حالا من ضمير اليوم المتقدم في مشهود، أو نعتا لأنه نكرة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows «لا تكلم نفس» as a circumstance of the Day in «يأتي», with «فيه» omitted, or as an adjective of «يوم يأتي»; the latter may mean a time rather than daytime.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: لا تكلم نفس، يصح أن يكون جملة في موضع الحال من الضمير الذي في يأتي

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya reconciles other Qurʾanic accounts of speech and argument at the Gathering with this verse by restricting them to God’s permission or to intercession and presenting a proof.
rows.anchor: وما ورد في القرآن من ذكر كلام أهل الموقف في التلازم والتساؤل والتجادل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Ibn ʿAtiyya’s parsing of «لا تكلم» appears borrowed from al-Hufi.
rows.anchor: وكلامه في إعراب لا تكلم كأنه منقول من كلام الحوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view describes Resurrection as a long Day with different stations: people sometimes argue, fall silent without permission, speak by permission, or have sealed mouths while limbs testify.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يوم القيامة يوم طويل له مواقف، ففي بعضها يجادلون عن أنفسهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes «منهم» to mean the people at the Gathering, understood from the no-speech statement and the earlier mention of people gathered.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الضمير لأهل الموقف

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says «منهم» returns to the collective conveyed by the generic word «نفس».
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: فمنهم عائد على الجميع الذي تضمنه قوله: نفس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines the wretched as those whose misery was written and the happy as those whose happiness was written.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الشقي من كتبت عليه الشقاوة، والسعيد الذي كتبت له السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses make the two groups the punished and blessed, or the deprived and provided for.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معذب ومنعم، وقيل: محروم ومرزوق

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the pronoun in «منهم» refers to the community of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes the exception as covering rational beings; those excluded from the Fire passage are sinful believers, while those excluded from Paradise are either they or the people of al-Aʿraf, who did not enter initially or remain as long as the first entrants.
rows.anchor: أو تكون واقعة على من يعقل على مذهب من يرى وقوعها على من يعقل مطلقا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers that the exception concerns remaining in the Fire’s punishment and Paradise’s delight, not final residence: Hell includes cold, other punishments, divine wrath and humiliation; Paradise includes divine pleasure and unquantifiable gifts beyond its reward.
rows.anchor: هو استثناء من الخلود في عذاب النار، ومن الخلود في نعيم أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He takes «إن ربك فعال لما يريد» as saying God inflicts the punishment He wills on Hell’s people and grants Paradise’s people an unending gift.
rows.anchor: أنه يفعل بأهل النار، ما يريد من العذاب، كما يعطي أهل الجنة عطاءه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects the claim that the exception releases major sinners from Hell through intercession, arguing that its second occurrence refutes that reading; he invokes a report from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr that Hell will one day be empty after its inmates remain there for ages, and condemns using it to deny disbelievers’ eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: قول المجبرة: المراد بالاستثناء خروج أهل الكبائر من النار بالشفاعة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: The report attributed to him says a day will come when Hell’s doors clap shut with no one inside, after its people have remained there for ages.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: ليأتين على جهنم يوم تصفق فيه أبوابها ليس فيها أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report from Abu al-ʿAs is authentic, Abu Hayyan says it means people leave the Fire for the cold of zamharir, making Hell empty and its doors shut.
rows.anchor: ولئن صح هذا عن أبي العاص فمعناه يخرجون من النار إلى برد الزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari’s exception can work for Hell if its people leave the Fire for zamharir, but his Paradise interpretation fails: receiving God’s pleasure and extra gifts does not stop them being eternal residents there.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذكره من الاستثناء في أهل الجنة من قوله: خالدين، فلا يتمشى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the exception may be a recommended qualification of any statement, like the promise to enter the Sacred Mosque “if God wills”; as a condition, it need not be classed as connected or disconnected.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وأما قوله إلا ما شاء ربك، فقيل فيه: إن ذلك على طريق الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya lists an interpretation in which the exception concerns the duration, based on reports that Hell will be destroyed, its inhabitants perish, and its doors clatter shut; Abu Hayyan calls this untenable.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو استثناء من طول المدة، وذلك على ما روي أن جهنم تخرب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿud and others that Hell empties is restricted to its upper level reserved for sinful believers; that level is called Jahannam, and the whole is named by it figuratively.
rows.anchor: والذي روي ونقل عن ابن مسعود وغيره: أنها تخلو من النار إنما هو الدرك الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed readings make «إلا» mean “and,” or “besides” as a disconnected exception; the latter means God adds what He wills and is attributed to al-Farraʾ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى الواو، فمعنى الآية: وما شاء الله زائدا على ذلك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ supports the disconnected “besides” interpretation by «عطاء غير مجذوذ»: an addition beyond their stated duration.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further proposals make the exception refer to additional unknown forms of punishment such as zamharir, to the span before the afterlife, to the barzakh, or to differences in the groups’ staggered entry into Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سوى ما أعد لهم من أنواع العذاب مما لا يعرف كالزمهرير

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A view transmitted by Abu Nuṣra from Jabir, or alternatively Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, takes the exception from «ففي النار»: God may delay some people’s entry into Hell.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول رواه أبو نصرة عن جابر، أو عن أبي سعيد الخدري

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abu Mujliz interprets the exception as God pardoning someone whose sin would otherwise merit eternal Hell, so that He does not put that person in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز: إلا ما شاء ربك أن يتجاوز عنه بعذاب يكون جزاؤه الخلود في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final gloss equates «إلا ما شاء ربك» with “as your Lord willed,” by analogy with «إلا ما قد سلف».
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى إلا ما شاء ربك كما شاء ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following statement that God does what He wills underscores His power.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر منبها على قدرة الله تعالى فقال: إن ربك فعال لما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports al-Hasan’s reading «شقوا» with a ḍamma on the shīn; the majority use a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: شقوا بضم الشين، والجمهور بفتحها

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Talha ibn Musarrif, Ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs read «سُعِدوا» with a ḍamma on the sīn; the remaining canonical readers and majority use a fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود، وطلحة بن مصرف، وابن وثاب، والأعمش، وحمزة، والكسائي، وحفص سعدوا بضم السين

rows.speaker: علي بن سليمان
rows.claim: Ali ibn Sulayman wondered that al-Kisaʾi, despite his Arabic expertise, read «سعدوا»; Abu Hayyan says there is no cause for surprise because it is transmitted from Ibn Masʿud and the other listed readers.
rows.anchor: وكان علي بن سليمان يتعجب من قراءة الكسائي سعدوا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi cites «مسعود» as support for «سعدوا»; Abu Hayyan objects that the adjective may mean “a place in which one was made happy,” with «فيه» omitted.
rows.anchor: وقد احتج الكسائي بقولهم: مسعود

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi treats «سعدوا» as based on «مسعود» but calls it rare and anomalous, since Arabic says «أسعده الله», not «سعده الله».
rows.anchor: وقال المهدوي: من قرأ سعدوا فهو محمول على مسعود، وهو شاذ قليل

rows.speaker: الثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says «سعد» and «أسعد» have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال الثعلبي: سعد وأسعد بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «عطاء» is an accusative verbal noun meaning “giving,” as in describing God’s causing people to grow from earth as “growth.”
rows.anchor: وانتصب عطاء على المصدر أي: أعطوا عطاء بمعنى إعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «غير مجذوذ» means uncut and continuing without end.
rows.anchor: ومعنى غير مجذوذ: غير مقطوع، بل هو ممتد إلى غير نهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A similar verse was explained earlier in al-Anʿam. Here «ليهلك» strengthens the negation: Kufans call the lām emphatic, while Basrans direct the negation to the omitted predicate governed by it.
rows.anchor: إلا أن هنا ليهلك وهي آكد في النفي

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits the reading “for their wrongdoing while they were reformers,” meaning they acted well and justly toward one another; that view requires their disbelief to have been accompanied by another sin.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: بشرك منهم وهم مصلحون أي: مصلحون في أعمالهم وسيرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya calls that view weak; its premise that states are spared for disbelief but not injustice should be reversed, since God would not punish a people for sins while they remain sound in faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا ضعيف، وإنما ذهب قائله إلى نحو ما قال

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers «بظلم» to mean an injustice from God, from which He is exalted.
rows.anchor: والذي رجح ابن عطية أن يكون التأويل بظلم منه تعالى عن ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says «وأهلها مصلحون» declares God free of injustice, since destroying reformers would itself be injustice.
rows.anchor: وأهلها مصلحون تنزيها لذاته عن الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says this clashes with the report that righteous people may perish when evil becomes widespread, and with the warning that a trial can strike beyond its wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وهو مصادم للحديث: «أنهلك وفينا الصالحون قال: نعم، إذا كثر الخبث»

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God could have compelled people into one religion, Islam, but instead they differ.
rows.anchor: يعني لاضطرارهم إلى أن يكونوا أهل ملة واحدة وهي ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take «ذلك» as the mercy in «إلا من رحم ربك» and the pronoun in «خلقهم» as those shown mercy.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: ذلك إشارة إلى الرحمة التي تضمنها قوله: إلا من رحم ربك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, chosen by al-Tabari, takes «ذلك» as both divergence and mercy, allowing one demonstrative to point to two things as in «عوان بين ذلك»; «خلقهم» refers to both groups.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، واختاره الطبري: الإشارة بذلك إلى الاختلاف والرحمة معا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes the antecedent of «خلقهم» to be the divergence among people.
rows.anchor: إلا الاختلاف كما قال الحسن وعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the only plausible antecedents of the pronoun are divergence, mercy, or both; interpretations beyond these reach too far.
rows.anchor: وليس في هذه الجملة ما يمكن أن يعود عليه الضمير إلا الاختلاف كما قال الحسن وعطاء، أو الرحمة كما قال مجاهد، وقتادة، أو كلاهما كما قال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A remote proposal points «ذلك» forward to the decree to fill Hell and says God created them for that purpose; Abu Hayyan rejects the syntax as highly implausible Arabic.
rows.anchor: وفيه تقديم وتأخير أي: وتمت كلمة ربك لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين، ولذلك خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed antecedents for «ذلك» are the witnessed Day, the wretched and happy groups, one group in Paradise and one in Hell, forbidding corruption, worship, Paradise and Hell, or felicity and misery; Abu Hayyan regards these as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إشارة إلى شهود ذلك اليوم المشهود، وقيل: إلى قوله: فمنهم شقي وسعيد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes «ولذلك» to point to the empowerment and choice implied by the discourse, which underlie divergence: people were created so right-choice is rewarded and wrong-choice punished; Abu Hayyan identifies this with Muʿtazilite theology.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما دل عليه الكلام أولا من التمكين والاختيار الذي عنه الاختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «تمت كلمة ربك» means God’s decree has come to pass and His command has taken effect.
rows.anchor: وتمت كلمة ربك أي: نفذ قضاؤه وحق أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in «لأملأن» introduces the oath’s response, or the preceding sentence implies an oath.
rows.anchor: واللام في لأملأن، هي التي يتلقى بها القسم، أو الجملة قبلها ضمنت معنى القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «الجنة» and «الجن» mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: والجنة والجن بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the hāʾ in «الجنة» intensifies the word; although «الجن» can be singular, «الجنة» is its collective plural.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والهاء فيه للمبالغة، وإن كان الجن يقع على الواحد، فالجنة جمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is like singular «كمء» and its plural «كمأة», where the collective is marked with hāʾ.
rows.anchor: كمء للواحد، وكمأة للجمع

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take “the truth in this” to refer to this sura and the verses recounting earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى السورة والآيات التي فيها تذكر قصص الأمم، وهذا قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although all the Qurʾan is true, this sura is singled out because its account warns disbelievers and alerts the observer: here is the truth that befell unjust peoples; the expression “the truth came” is especially used in calamity.
rows.anchor: ووجه تخصيص هذه السورة بوصفها بالحق، والقرآن كله حق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada take the reference as the abode of this world; Qatada further identifies “the truth” as prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: الإشارة إلى دار الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses «الحق» as prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: والحق النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the reference as this sura together with similar suras.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إشارة إلى السورة مع نظائرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands to work and wait are threats and warnings addressed to the people of Mecca and others; «على مكانتكم» means in the direction or condition they have chosen.
rows.anchor: اعملوا صيغة أمر ومعناه: التهديد والوعيد، والخطاب لأهل مكة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading means: do what you can to destroy me and await reversals for us; we await a punishment like that inflicted on your earlier counterparts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اعملوا في هلاكي على إمكانكم، وانتظروا بنا الدوائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands may signal a truce, which led some to say these verses were abrogated; others hold them operative as threats while hostilities continue.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون إيتاء موادعة، فلذلك قيل: إنهما منسوختان، وقيل: محكمتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows the unseen of the heavens and earth; no creature has a share in unseen knowledge, and the whole affair returns to Him.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء من أعمالكم، ولا حظ لمخلوق في علم الغيب

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Hafs read «يرجع» in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحفص: يرجع مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: «الأمر كله» means their affairs and yours; God will take vengeance on them for you.
rows.anchor: الأمر كله أمرهم وأمرك، فينتقم لك منهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi says the phrase means knowledge of what is unseen in the heavens and earth, with “unseen” attributed to them by extension.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: علم ما غاب في السموات والأرض، أضاف الغيب إليهما توسعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause indicates God’s comprehensive knowledge of all beings, universals and particulars, present and absent; if He knows what is unseen, He also knows what is present, since His knowledge does not vary.
rows.anchor: دلت على أن علمه محيط بجميع الكائنات كليها وجزئيها حاضرها وغائبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause indicates God’s effective power and will.
rows.anchor: والجملة الثانية: دلت على القدرة النافذة والمشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third clause commands bodily and inward worship of the One with these attributes; worship is the servant’s highest rank.
rows.anchor: والجملة الثالثة: دلت على الأمر بإفراد من هذه صفاته بالعبادة الجسدية والقلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth clause commands reliance on God: worship reveals that all things are attached to Him and under His sole direction, so the servant entrusts himself to Him and abandons imagined independent causes.
rows.anchor: والجملة الرابعة: دلت على الأمر بالتوكل، وهي آخرة الرتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth clause warns of recompense: no obedient person’s obedience is lost and no defiant person is neglected.
rows.anchor: والجملة الخامسة: تضمنت التنبيه على المجازاة، فلا يضيع طاعة مطيع ولا يهمل حال متمرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports that the two Kufan readers, Hafs, Qatada, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, Abu Jaʿfar, and al-Jahdari read «تعملون» with second-person address, matching the preceding command «اعملوا».
rows.anchor: تعملون بتاء الخطاب، لأن قبله اعملوا على مكانتكم

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The remaining canonical readers use third-person «يعملون»; the reading is also reported with variation from al-Hasan and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: بالياء على الغيبة، واختلف عن الحسن وعيسى بن عمر
